summary: Partial second checkpoint: 85 items (8 exact pinned-library imports, 35 inherited planned items, 42 missing). All 72 inherited item objects and their two routes are preserved. The new spectral-radius layer imports Mathlib smoothingFun rather than rebuilding it or confusing it with the minpoly-based spectralNorm. Four valid comparison lemmas have complete mathematical proofs but explicitly pending generic ownership; one unrouted diagnostic records the stronger false norm-uniqueness assertion in source issue E1. This is not full extraction, a final routing decision, an independent review or a Lean implementation.

items.name: An almost base with a flat tensor square
items.statement: An almost base is a commutative ring V with an ideal m satisfying m²=m and such that m⊗_V m is flat over V. The ideal m is an explicit input; it need not be a valuation-ring maximal ideal.

items.name: Base change of the almost-base condition
items.statement: For an almost base (V,m) and a ring map V→V′, the extended ideal mV′ is idempotent and its tensor square over V′ is flat.

items.name: Flat compatible-root ideals
items.statement: If π is a non-zero-divisor in V with a chosen compatible system π^(1/p^n), the ideal generated by all π^(1/p^n) is flat and idempotent; in particular it satisfies the almost-base condition.

items.name: The almost-module category
items.statement: For an almost base (V,m), form Vᵃ-Mod by localizing V-Mod at morphisms whose kernel and cokernel are killed by m, equivalently the Serre quotient by modules M with mM=0. This is an abelian category.

items.name: Almost injectivity, surjectivity and isomorphisms
items.statement: A V-linear map is almost injective, almost surjective, or an almost isomorphism when its kernel, cokernel, or both, respectively, are annihilated by m. These correspond to monomorphisms, epimorphisms, and isomorphisms after almostification.

items.name: Almostification and its two module adjoints
items.statement: Writing m̃=m⊗_V m, the exact localization M↦Mᵃ has right adjoint N↦N_*=Hom_{Vᵃ}(Vᵃ,N) and left adjoint N↦N_!=m̃⊗_V N_*. One has (N_*)ᵃ≅N, (Mᵃ)_*≅Hom_V(m̃,M), and Hom_{Vᵃ}(Mᵃ,Nᵃ)≅Hom_V(m̃⊗_V M,N). Almostification preserves limits and colimits.

items.name: Detecting almost epimorphisms on almost elements
items.statement: For a morphism N→N′ of almost V-modules, the morphism is an epimorphism if and only if N_*→N′_* is almost surjective. The right adjoint (-)_* is not asserted to be right exact.

items.name: Mittag–Leffler for almost modules
items.statement: For an inverse sequence (N_n) of almost V-modules with epimorphic transition maps, lim_n N_n→N_0 is an epimorphism.

items.name: Countable derived inverse limits
items.statement: The almost-module category is complete and cocomplete and products preserve epimorphisms. For inverse sequences, and hence inverse systems admitting a countable cofinal chain, higher inverse limits vanish in degrees greater than one. Almostification commutes with lim¹, computed by the usual product telescope cokernel.

items.name: Adically complete almost Nakayama
items.statement: Let I be an ideal of V and f:M→N a morphism of I-adically complete almost V-modules. If M/IM→N/IN is an epimorphism, then f is an epimorphism. The proof uses the graded pieces, surjectivity on the kernels of successive quotients, and almost Mittag–Leffler.

items.name: Almost algebras and module categories
items.statement: Almost V-algebras are commutative monoid objects of Vᵃ-Mod. For an almost algebra A construct A-Mod, A-Alg and the relative tensor product. Almostification on algebras has the right adjoint (-)_* and a left adjoint (-)_!!; the latter is distinct from the module left adjoint.

items.name: Limits, coproducts and idempotents for almost algebras
items.statement: Almost-algebra categories have small limits and colimits. Relative tensor products are coproducts, and (B⊗_A C)ᵃ≅Bᵃ⊗_{Aᵃ}Cᵃ for ordinary V-algebras. Finite product decompositions are described by complete orthogonal idempotent systems in the ring of almost elements.

items.name: Extensions of almost algebras
items.statement: A morphism A→B of almost V-algebras is a monomorphism precisely when A_*→B_* is almost injective. Such monomorphisms are the extensions used in the almost Galois arguments.

items.name: Changing the almost base
items.statement: For a ring map V→V′ carrying m into m′, restriction of scalars induces exact functors from (V′,m′)ᵃ-modules to (V,m)ᵃ-modules and corresponding functors on almost algebras and their module categories. For the relative categories on a fixed underlying algebra these are equivalences when the image of m generates m′. Include the natural comparison of almost-element functors.

items.name: Flat and faithfully flat almost modules and maps
items.statement: An almost A-module M is flat when -⊗_A M is exact. A→B is faithfully flat when extension of scalars is exact and faithful. Equivalently for a map of almost algebras, it is a monomorphism and B/A is flat.

items.name: Transport and filtered colimits of almost flat extensions
items.statement: Flatness or faithful flatness of A_*→B_* implies the corresponding almost property; faithful flatness is equivalent to faithful flatness for the algebra left-adjoint map. Filtered colimits of flat, respectively faithfully flat, extensions retain the corresponding property.

items.name: Almost finite projectivity by approximate retracts
items.statement: An almost A-module P is finite projective in André’s convention if, for every η∈m, there are n and maps P→A^n→P whose composite is η·id_P. This is the almost, not ordinary, finite-projective condition.

items.name: Homological characterization of almost finite projectivity
items.statement: The approximate-retract condition is equivalent to almost projectivity, expressed by annihilation by m of all positive Ext groups into any module, together with almost finite generation: for every η∈m there is A^n→P with cokernel killed by η.

items.name: Flatness of almost projective modules
items.statement: Every almost projective module is flat. A faithful almost projective A-module, with faithfulness defined by the monomorphism A→End(P)ᵃ, is faithfully flat.

items.name: Exterior powers and trace for almost finite projectives
items.statement: Exterior powers of an almost finite-projective A-module remain almost finite projective. Construct its trace morphism (End P)ᵃ→A and define constant rank r by Λ^(r+1)P=0 and invertibility of Λ^r P.

items.name: Faithfully flat descent of almost finite projectivity
items.statement: For a faithfully flat map A→A′ of almost algebras, P is almost finite projective over A if and only if P⊗_A A′ is almost finite projective over A′.

items.name: Completeness of almost finite projective modules
items.statement: If the almost algebra A is I-adically complete, every almost finite-projective A-module P is I-adically complete. The comparison P→lim_n P/I^nP has kernel and cokernel annihilated by every η∈m via approximate finite-free retracts.

items.name: Almost finite étale algebras
items.statement: An almost A-algebra B is finite étale when B is almost finite projective over A and multiplication B⊗_A B→B is projection onto a factor in a decomposition B⊗_A B≅B×C. Under finite projectivity the second condition is equivalent to flatness of multiplication.

items.name: Trace pairing for almost finite étale algebras
items.statement: For an almost finite étale A-algebra B, trace is compatible with base change and the pairing (b,c)↦Tr(bc) identifies B with its A-dual. If A→B is an extension, it is faithfully flat and trace is an epimorphism.

items.name: Faithfully flat descent of almost finite étaleness
items.statement: For a faithfully flat map A→A′ of almost algebras, B is almost finite étale over A if and only if B⊗_A A′ is almost finite étale over A′. The assertion also preserves a specified constant rank.

items.name: Reduction equivalence with its restricted almost ideal
items.statement: If m=π^(1/p^∞)V and the almost algebra A is π-adically complete, reduction modulo π is an equivalence from almost finite étale A-algebras to almost finite étale A/π-algebras. The special form of the almost ideal is part of the hypothesis and cannot be dropped in the ramified (ϖT) setting.

items.name: The finite Galois comparison map
items.statement: For a finite group G acting by A-algebra automorphisms of an almost A-algebra B, construct B⊗_A B→∏_{γ∈G}B by b⊗b′↦(γ(b)b′)_γ and the invariant almost algebra B^G as an equalizer.

items.name: Almost Galois extensions
items.statement: An extension A→B with a given finite group G of A-automorphisms is G-Galois if B^G=A and the comparison B⊗_A B→∏_G B is an isomorphism. These conditions may be tested with the right adjoint (-)_*, but do not imply that A_*→B_* is an ordinary Galois extension.

items.name: Almost Galois implies almost finite étale
items.statement: A G-Galois extension of almost algebras is almost finite étale of constant rank |G|. Its trace is the sum of the G-conjugates. The proof extracts η-scaled dual bases from the torsor idempotent for every η∈m.

items.name: Base change and descent of almost Galois extensions
items.statement: A G-Galois extension A→B stays G-Galois after arbitrary almost-algebra base change A→A′. Conversely, G-Galoisness descends along faithfully flat A→A′.

items.name: Intermediate almost Galois extensions
items.statement: Let A→B be G-Galois and A→C→B intermediate, with C→B H-Galois for H⊂G. Then C⊗_A B≅∏_{G/H}B, and C is almost finite étale of constant rank |G/H| over A.

items.name: A symmetric-group Galois envelope
items.statement: For an injective finite étale ring map R→S of positive constant rank r, construct R→T that is S_r-Galois and factors through S, such that S→T is S_(r−1)-Galois. Geometrically remove all partial diagonals from the r-fold fibre power of Spec S over Spec R.
items.note: An explicit auxiliary construction for the finite étale descent proof owned by P3. The extension and positive-rank hypotheses prevent misuse of the rank-zero factor; it is not a primitive field normal-closure theorem.

items.name: Rigidity inside a ring with a finite group action
items.statement: Let a finite group G act on a ring S and set R=S^G. If a G-stable intermediate subring R⊂S′⊂S is G-Galois over R, then S′=S.
items.note: Supplies the finite étale/Galois proof step of P3; it is also used in Proposition 4.4.4(3). The proof uses faithful-flat descent, not a dimension argument.

items.name: Almost morphisms between uniform Banach algebras
items.statement: For an almost-perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra A, the category A^â-uBan has uniform Banach A-algebras as objects and Hom(B,C)=Hom_{A°ᵃ-Alg}(B°ᵃ,C°ᵃ). Its full subcategory A^â-pPerf consists of the almost-perfectoid objects. Here almostification uses the ideal generated by T^(1/p^n)K°° in the integral perfected-coordinate base.

items.name: Almost-perfectoid algebras
items.statement: A uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra B is almost perfectoid when B^â is isomorphic, in the category whose morphisms are maps between almost power-bounded algebras, to the image of a perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra. This does not assert that B itself is perfectoid.

items.name: Perfectoid coreflection after almostification
items.statement: The right adjoint B↦B^♮ to the inclusion of perfectoid algebras into uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebras induces a right adjoint after almostification. Restricted to almost-perfectoid objects, it is quasi-inverse to the inclusion of the almostified perfectoid category. The counit goes from B^♮ to B, not from B to B^♮.

items.name: Frobenius criterion for almost perfectoidness
items.statement: Let B be a uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra, and choose 0≠ϖ∈K°° with compatible p-power roots and |p|≤|ϖ|. Then B is almost perfectoid if and only if Frobenius on B°/ϖ is almost surjective for the ramified root ideal. Surjectivity here is equivalently almost surjectivity of the Frobenius-linearized module map, not an assertion that Frobenius is K°/ϖ-linear.

items.name: Integral counit criterion for almost perfectoidness
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 3.5.4, B is almost perfectoid if and only if (B^♮)°→B° is an almost isomorphism for the ramified root ideal.

items.name: Banach counit criterion for almost perfectoidness
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 3.5.4, B is almost perfectoid if and only if B^♮→B is an almost isomorphism, equivalently if some perfectoid Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra admits an almost-isomorphic continuous homomorphism to B.

items.name: Finite-group invariants of a perfectoid algebra
items.statement: If a finite group G acts on a perfectoid K-algebra B by continuous K-algebra automorphisms, the invariant algebra B^G, with its induced Banach topology, is perfectoid. No assumption that |G| is invertible is imposed.

items.name: Tilting commutes with finite-group invariants
items.statement: For a finite group G acting continuously on a perfectoid K-algebra B, the canonical comparison (B^G)^♭→(B^♭)^G is an isomorphism of perfectoid K^♭-algebras.

items.name: Integral root-localization models
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid of residue characteristic p, with 0≠ϖ∈K°°, |p|≤|ϖ|, and compatible p-power roots. For r∈N[1/p] and a (K°/ϖ^r)[T^(1/p^∞)]-algebra R, set R[j]=R⊗_{K°[T^(1/p^∞)]}K°[T^(1/p^∞),(ϖ^j/T)^(1/p^∞)]. The transition R[j+1]→R[j] sends (ϖ^(j+1)/T)^s to ϖ^s(ϖ^j/T)^s for s∈N[1/p]. The coefficient ring on the right is the indicated subring of the Laurent perfected-coordinate algebra, not a completion.

items.name: Recovery from integral root-localization models
items.statement: For R and R[j] as in §4.2.1, the canonical map R→lim_j R[j] is an almost isomorphism for the base (K°[T^(1/p^∞)],(ϖT)^(1/p^∞)). No flatness assumption on R over the coordinate ring is added.

items.name: Compatible-root saturation
items.statement: For a uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra A with g=T·1 a non-zero-divisor, define g^(-1/p^∞)A°={x∈A[1/g] : g^(1/p^n)x∈A° for every n≥0}=⋂_n g^(-1/p^n)A°. This is an intersection, not the union of the fractional lattices.

items.name: Perfectoid Riemann extension by an inverse limit
items.statement: Let A be an almost-perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra and g=T·1 a non-zero-divisor. With A[j]=A{ϖ^j/g}, the canonical comparison identifies lim_j A[j]° with g^(-1/p^∞)A°. The rational localizations carry their complete Banach topology; they are not the uncompleted algebraic localization A[1/g].

items.name: Root saturation as complete integral closure
items.statement: With A and g as in Theorem 4.2.2, g^(-1/p^∞)A° is the complete integral closure of A° in A[1/g]. Complete integral closure means closure under almost-integral elements, not merely topological closure or ordinary integral closure.

items.name: Largest perfectoid subalgebra in a principal localization
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 4.2.2, (g^(-1/p^∞)A°[1/ϖ])^♮ is the largest spectral perfectoid A-algebra contained in A[1/g] with continuous structure map. The perfectoid coreflection is part of this formula; it must not be silently removed.

items.name: Tilting the root-saturated integral algebra
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Corollary 4.2.4, let g^♭ be the element of A^♭ corresponding to the compatible roots of g. There is a canonical identification (g^(-1/p^∞)A°)^♭=(g^♭)^(-1/p^∞)(A^♭)°. This identifies the tilted integral algebra, without asserting that g^(-1/p^∞)A°[1/ϖ] is itself perfectoid in mixed characteristic.

items.name: Uniform inverse limit
items.statement: For an inverse system of uniform Banach K-algebras (A_α), its uniform inverse limit is the bounded inverse limit: A=(lim_α A_α°)[1/ϖ] with the topology defined by the integral inverse limit. For perfectoid A_α its perfectoid-category limit A′ has a canonical map A′→A. These limits are distinct constructions.
items.note: This checkpoint fixes the construction consumed by the ramified theorem. Its general Banach-category ownership must be reconciled with AdicSpacesPartII before the extraction is completed; the Part II route must import any existing general supplier.

items.name: When a uniform inverse limit is the perfectoid limit
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid of characteristic zero, let (A_α) be an inverse system of perfectoid K-algebras, and let A′→A be the comparison from its perfectoid limit to its uniform limit. Then A is perfectoid if and only if A′→A is an isomorphism.

items.name: An integral inverse-limit criterion for perfectoidness
items.statement: In Proposition 4.3.1 choose 0≠ϖ∈K°° with pK°⊂ϖK° and an element denoted ϖ^(1/p) of norm |ϖ|^(1/p). If lim_α(A_α°/ϖ)→lim_α(A_α°/ϖ^(1/p)) is almost surjective for (K°,K°°), then the uniform limit A is perfectoid. This is a sufficient condition; the proposition does not claim its necessity.

items.name: Ramified almost-perfectoid inverse-limit criterion
items.statement: Let (A_α) be an inverse system of perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebras in the characteristic-zero setting of Proposition 4.3.1, and A its uniform limit. If lim_α(A_α°/ϖ)→lim_α(A_α°/ϖ^(1/p)) is almost surjective for the ideal T^(1/p^∞)K°°, then A^♮→A is an almost isomorphism; hence A is almost perfectoid.

items.name: Integral reduction of the ramified uniform limit
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of the ramified almost-perfectoid inverse-limit criterion in Remark 4.3.1, the map A°/ϖ→lim_α(A_α°/ϖ) is an almost isomorphism for the same ramified ideal.

items.name: Vanishing of the nested root-localization lim¹
items.statement: Use the root-localization construction R↦R[j] of §4.2.1. If (R_i) is an inverse sequence of (K°/ϖ^r)[T^(1/p^∞)]-algebras such that R_i[j]→R_j[j]←R_j are almost isomorphisms for every i≥j, then lim¹_j(R_jᵃ)=0 in the ramified almost category. The proof uses summable annihilator estimates, not an assumption that all transition maps are surjective.

items.name: Compatible perfectoid algebras on principal annuli
items.statement: For an almost-perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra A, set A[j]=A{ϖ^j/g}. Form the category of inverse systems of perfectoid A[j]-algebras B_j for which B_i{ϖ^j/g}→B_j is an isomorphism whenever i≥j; morphisms are compatible algebra morphisms. Rational localization defines σ from A^â-pPerf to this category.

items.name: Almost perfectoidness of compatible annular limits
items.statement: For an object (B_j) of the compatible annular category in §4.4.2, its uniform inverse limit is an almost-perfectoid A-algebra. Perfectoidness without almostification is not asserted.

items.name: Localization and uniform-limit adjunction
items.statement: For the categories of §4.4.2, uniform inverse limit is right adjoint to σ. The unit is an isomorphism: ulim∘σ≅id on A^â-pPerf. Consequently σ is fully faithful. The theorem does not assert that σ is essentially surjective.

items.name: Annular tower from a finite étale punctured algebra
items.statement: Let A be as in §4.4.2 and B′ a finite étale A[1/g]-algebra. Give B_j=B′⊗_{A[1/g]}A[j] its canonical finite étale Banach topology. Each B_j is perfectoid and the system belongs to the compatible annular category.

items.name: Recovering the annular pieces of the finite étale envelope
items.statement: Let B′ and B_j be as in Proposition 4.4.4 and B=ulim_j B_j. Then the canonical comparison B{ϖ^j/g}→B_j is an isomorphism for every j. This effectivity assertion is for towers arising from B′, not for every compatible annular tower.

items.name: Recovering the punctured finite étale algebra
items.statement: With B=ulim_j(B′⊗_{A[1/g]}A[j]) as in Proposition 4.4.4, the canonical map B′→B[1/g] is an isomorphism. Its proof uses the perfect trace pairing for injectivity and the finite Galois-envelope argument for surjectivity.

items.name: The ramified almost base for Abhyankar’s lemma
items.statement: Fix a perfectoid field K of residue characteristic p and 0≠ϖ∈K°° with compatible p-power roots and |p|≤|ϖ|. Use V=K°[T^(1/p^∞)] and m=(ϖT)^(1/p^∞)V. For a K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra A put g=T·1. Statements using this almost base differ from statements using (K°,K°°), even though the two compare after g is inverted.

items.name: Ramified almost-perfectoid extension equivalence
items.statement: In the base of §5.1, let A be an almost-perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra and g=T·1. Inverting g is an equivalence from A^â-algebras that are almost perfectoid and finite étale after inverting g to finite étale A[1/g]-algebras. A quasi-inverse sends B′ to ulim_j(B′⊗_{A[1/g]}A{ϖ^j/g}); the unit and counit are the identifications proved in §§4.4–5.2.

items.name: Integral form of ramified extension
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 5.2.1, inverting ϖ gives an equivalence between complete A°ᵃ-algebras that are finite étale modulo every power p^m and finite étale after inverting g, and A^â-algebras that are almost perfectoid and finite étale after inverting g. The quasi-inverse is the almost power-bounded algebra. The source’s condition is finite étale modulo every p^m; it is not replaced by integral almost finite étaleness.

items.name: Almost finite étaleness modulo powers of p
items.statement: In the base of §5.1 let A be almost perfectoid and let B be a perfectoid A-algebra in which g is a non-zero-divisor. Assume B[1/g] is finite étale over A[1/g]. Then B°ᵃ/p^m is finite étale over A°ᵃ/p^m for every m∈N, using the ramified almost ideal (ϖT)^(1/p^∞).

items.name: Integral almost purity after inverting the discriminant
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 5.2.3, B°[1/g] is almost finite étale over A°[1/g] in the valuation-ring almost setting (K°,K°°). This uses a different almost ideal from the modulo-p^m assertion.

items.name: Root-saturated integral envelope of a finite étale algebra
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra, g=T·1 a non-zero-divisor, and B′ finite étale over A[1/g]. Put S=g^(-1/p^∞)A°. Define D° as the ordinary integral closure of S in B′ and D as the ordinary integral closure of S[1/ϖ] in B′. These constructions are over the given A-algebra map; that map is not assumed injective when B′ is not faithful.

items.name: Identification of the analytic and integral envelopes
items.statement: In the setting of §5.3, let C=ulim_j(B′⊗_{A[1/g]}A{ϖ^j/g}). Then C=D and C°=D°. This identifies an almost-perfectoid envelope; its perfectoid coreflection is a separate object.

items.name: Completeness of the integral envelope
items.statement: The ring D° of §5.3 is ϖ-adically complete. It is the ordinary integral closure of g^(-1/p^∞)A° in B′, with the inherited topology supplied by its identification with the power-bounded ring of the uniform limit.

items.name: Root saturation of the integral envelope
items.statement: For D° as in §5.3, D°=(ϖg)^(-1/p^∞)D° inside B′, with root saturation interpreted as an intersection of fractional lattices.

items.name: Comparison with the ordinary integral closure of A°
items.statement: The inclusion of the ordinary integral closure of A° in B′ into D° is an almost isomorphism for (K°[T^(1/p^∞)],T^(1/p^∞)K°°[T^(1/p^∞)]).

items.name: The maximal perfectoid Abhyankar envelope
items.statement: For D of §5.3, D^♮ is the largest perfectoid A-algebra contained in B′, with continuous A-algebra structure. Its localization after inverting g is B′. The maximal object is D^♮, not an assertion that the almost-perfectoid algebra D itself is perfectoid.

items.name: Almost-surjectivity of the ramified trace
items.statement: In the setting of §5.3 assume in addition that B′ is faithful as an A[1/g]-module. Then Tr_{B′/A[1/g]}(D°)⊂g^(-1/p^∞)A° is an almost isomorphism of modules for the ramified almost base. Equivalently the trace map on D° is almost surjective onto that root-saturated integral ring.

items.name: Spectral-radius function from an existing ring seminorm
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and ring seminorm μ, put ρ_μ(x)=inf_{n≥1} μ(x^n)^(1/n). Use Mathlib smoothingFun on μ; the infimum is indexed by positive natural numbers, not by n=0.
items.locator: Published §2.2.1, p.13; pinned SmoothingSeminorm.lean as detailed in the second-checkpoint report
items.note: Actual declarations read at the prescribed pin. API: reuse RingSeminorm and smoothingFun, its positive-index infimum and the separate natural-number sequence used for convergence. No new spectral-radius carrier. Tests: (1) a multiplicative norm is fixed; (2) a nonzero square-zero element has radius zero; (3) n=0 is not admitted in the infimum. The minpoly-based spectralNorm for algebraic field extensions is not this definition.

items.name: Existence of the spectral-radius limit
items.statement: If μ is a ring seminorm on a commutative ring and μ(1)≤1, then μ(x^n)^(1/n) tends to ρ_μ(x) as n tends to infinity, for every x. No completeness or nonarchimedean hypothesis is needed by the cited declaration.
items.locator: Published §2.2.1, p.13; pinned SmoothingSeminorm.lean as detailed in the second-checkpoint report

items.name: Spectral radius is bounded by the original seminorm
items.statement: For any ring seminorm μ on a commutative ring and any x, ρ_μ(x)≤μ(x).
items.locator: Published §2.2.1, p.13; pinned SmoothingSeminorm.lean as detailed in the second-checkpoint report

items.name: The smoothed ring seminorm
items.statement: If μ(1)≤1 and μ is a nonarchimedean ring seminorm on a commutative ring R, smoothingSeminorm μ is a ring seminorm on R whose underlying function is ρ_μ.
items.locator: Published §2.2.1, p.13; pinned SmoothingSeminorm.lean as detailed in the second-checkpoint report
items.note: The hypotheses and constructor fields were read at the pin. This alone does not assert separation, K-scalar homogeneity or completeness. API: reuse the RingSeminorm structure, its evaluation as smoothingFun and existing zero, negation, addition and multiplication inequalities. Tests: (1) nilpotents may be in the kernel; (2) the zero ring and zero seminorm are allowed; (3) the max norm on a product is not generally multiplicative.

items.name: The spectral-radius function is nonarchimedean
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean ring seminorm μ with μ(1)≤1 on a commutative ring, ρ_μ(x+y)≤max(ρ_μ(x),ρ_μ(y)).
items.locator: Published §2.2.1, p.13; pinned SmoothingSeminorm.lean as detailed in the second-checkpoint report

items.name: Power multiplicativity of spectral radius
items.statement: For a ring seminorm μ with μ(1)≤1 on a commutative ring, ρ_μ(x^m)=ρ_μ(x)^m for every positive integer m. The actual cited declaration does not require the extra nonarchimedean hypothesis mentioned in its prose comment.
items.locator: Published §2.2.1, p.13; pinned SmoothingSeminorm.lean as detailed in the second-checkpoint report

items.name: An already power-multiplicative seminorm is fixed
items.statement: Let μ be a ring seminorm with μ(1)≤1. If μ(x^n)=μ(x)^n for every positive n, then ρ_μ(x)=μ(x). In particular smoothing fixes any power-multiplicative norm pointwise.
items.locator: Published §2.2.1, p.13; pinned SmoothingSeminorm.lean as detailed in the second-checkpoint report

items.name: Smoothing preserves multiplication by a multiplicative element
items.statement: Let μ be a ring seminorm with μ(1)≤1. If x satisfies μ(xy)=μ(x)μ(y) for every y, then ρ_μ(xy)=ρ_μ(x)ρ_μ(y) for every y. In addition ρ_μ(x)=μ(x).
items.locator: Published §2.2.1, p.13; pinned SmoothingSeminorm.lean as detailed in the second-checkpoint report
items.note: This is the exact generic input for scalar homogeneity, not a claim that the full normed K-algebra wrapper is already packaged. Both component declarations were read at the pin; the preservation equation is the primary extracted result and the normalization is its required interface.

items.name: A bounded homomorphism contracts spectral radii
items.statement: Let R,S be commutative rings with ring seminorms μ,ν satisfying μ(1)≤1 and ν(1)≤1. Let f:R→S be a ring homomorphism and suppose ν(f(x))≤Cμ(x) for every x, for some real C>0. Then ρ_ν(f(x))≤ρ_μ(x) for every x.
items.locator: Published §2.2.4, p.13; elementary general ring-seminorm formulation and proof in the second-checkpoint report
items.note: Direct proof in the second-checkpoint report: apply the bound to x^n, take positive nth roots and pass to the imported limits, using C^(1/n)→1. No completeness or injectivity is needed. Reuse the ring-homomorphism and smoothing APIs. The exact packaged theorem has not been located at the pins; generic-supplier routing is explicitly pending, not silently assigned to PerfectoidRamification.

items.name: Equivalent seminorms have the same spectral-radius function
items.statement: For ring seminorms μ,ν on a commutative ring with μ(1),ν(1)≤1, suppose ν≤Cμ and μ≤Dν pointwise for positive constants C,D. Then ρ_μ=ρ_ν pointwise.
items.locator: Published §2.2.4, p.13; valid equivalence-of-norms argument, expanded in the second-checkpoint report
items.note: Apply bounded-map-contraction to the identity in both directions. Neither completeness nor separation is required. Explicit constants are part of the hypothesis; arbitrary norms on the same algebra need not satisfy it. Exact generic declaration matching and final ownership remain pending.

items.name: Uniqueness of a spectral norm for a fixed topology
items.statement: Let K be a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field and A a commutative K-algebra. Two power-multiplicative K-algebra norms which induce the same topology on A are equal. Completeness of A is not required.
items.note: Continuity of each identity K-linear map gives a uniform norm bound using a scalar π with 0<|π|<1. Then use equivalent-spectral-functions and spectral-fixed. Full scalar-rescaling proof is in the report. This statement retains the topology hypothesis and is not the false abstract-algebra assertion in E1. Reuse the existing normed-linear-map interfaces; the exact packaged comparison remains unaudited.

items.name: Uniqueness under one continuous identity and two complete norms
items.statement: Let K be a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field and A a commutative K-algebra with two complete power-multiplicative K-algebra norms. If the identity from the first norm topology to the second is continuous, the norms are equal.
items.locator: Corrected replacement for the second paragraph of published §2.2.4, p.13; not a verbatim source theorem
items.note: The continuous identity is a bijective bounded K-linear map between complete Hausdorff normed K-vector spaces. Apply the existing open-mapping supplier to make its inverse continuous, then fixed-topology-uniqueness. Do not replace either norm by their maximum without independently proving that the resulting norm is complete. Foundations of adic spaces Layer 0.6 is a read supplier for open mapping, not a new source route that rewrites an upstream roadmap. Final ownership of the small Banach comparison package remains pending.

items.name: Diagnostic: uniqueness from completeness alone on an abstract algebra
items.statement: The source asserts that a K-algebra has at most one spectral norm making it complete, without fixing its topology or assuming continuity of the identity. Source issue E1 records a counterexample on the abstract Q_p-algebra C_p and the failure of completeness for the maximum norm. This literal assertion is not an accepted theorem target.
items.locator: Published §2.2.4, second paragraph, p.13; same claim in arXiv:1609.00320v1 §2.2.4, p.12
items.note: Unrouted diagnostic. The algebraic automorphism used in E1 fixes the dense subfield Q_p-bar but is not continuous. Its two pulled-back norms are separately complete and multiplicative. Independent review has not yet confirmed this finding; neither failure of the main Abhyankar theorem nor a complete audit of all downstream uses is claimed.

items.name: Semi-norm and norm of a K-algebra
items.statement: K is complete for a non-trivial non-archimedean absolute value, with valuation ring K°, valuation ideal K°° and residue field k. A K-algebra semi-norm is |·|:A→R with |a+b|≤max(|a|,|b|), |ab|≤|a||b| with equality when a∈K, and |1|=1 for A≠0; it is a norm if it vanishes only at 0. A_{≤r} and A_{<r} are the corresponding subsets, and the unit ball A_{≤1} is an open K°-subalgebra. All algebras are commutative unital, and the zero algebra is not excluded.

items.name: A multiplicative norm forces a domain
items.statement: A K-algebra carrying a multiplicative norm is an integral domain.

items.name: Normed K-algebras, K-Ban, and continuous morphisms
items.statement: Morphisms of normed K-algebras are the continuous algebra homomorphisms, equivalently those bounded on A_{≤1}, equivalently those with ‖φ‖ = sup_{a≠0}|φ(a)|/|a| < ∞; φ is isometric if |φ(a)|=|a| for all a. K-Ban is the full subcategory of complete objects; for A∈K-Ban the A-Banach algebras form A-Ban.

items.name: K-Ban has finite limits and finite colimits
items.statement: K-Ban has initial object K, final object 0, amalgamated sums B⊗̂_A C (the separated completion of B⊗_A C for the tensor-product semi-norm) and fibre products B×_A C, hence finite colimits and finite limits. The functor −⊗̂_K A is left adjoint to the forgetful functor A-Ban → K-Ban.

items.name: Quotients of a completed tensor product by closed ideals
items.statement: For I a closed ideal of B and J a closed ideal of C, and 𝔎 the closure of the image of I⊗C+B⊗J in B⊗̂_A C, the canonical morphism (B⊗̂_A C)/𝔎 → (B/I)⊗̂_A(C/J) is an isometry (2.1).

items.name: Completeness of B⊗_A C for C finite projective
items.statement: If C is finite projective over A and its norm induces the canonical topology of a finite projective A-module, then B⊗_A C is already complete. This fails in general for C finite but not projective.

items.name: Orthogonal bases compute the norm of a completed tensor product
items.statement: If C has an orthogonal basis (c_j) over A then every d∈B⊗̂_A C is uniquely d=Σb_j⊗c_j with |d|=max_j|b_j||c_j|; consequently b↦b⊗1 embeds B isometrically in B⊗̂_A C. A normed A-subalgebra C′⊆C need not give a normed subalgebra B⊗̂_A C′ ⊆ B⊗̂_A C.

items.name: Power-bounded and topologically nilpotent elements
items.statement: A° is the set of elements with bounded powers: an open K°-subalgebra containing A_{≤1}, depending only on the equivalence class of the norm, functorial and commuting with completion, with (A×B)°=A°×B°. A°° is the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements, open in A° and equal to its own radical. For A complete, A°° lies in the Jacobson radical of A°, so an element of A° is invertible iff its image in A°/A°° is, and the maximal ideals of A are closed. A↦A°/A°° is a functor to reduced k-algebras.

items.name: The Tate algebra A⟨T⟩ and its universal property
items.statement: A⟨T⟩ is the completion of A[T] for the Gauss norm (the supremum of the coefficient norms), which is multiplicative if that of A is; then A⟨T⟩° is the algebra of convergent series with coefficients in A°, and (A⟨T⟩,T) is universal among pairs (B,b∈B°) with B an A-Banach algebra.

items.name: The contractive subcategory and the isometry (2.2)
items.statement: In the non-full subcategory of K-Ban with the same objects and the morphisms of norm ≤1, in which ⊗̂ is still a coproduct, (A⟨T⟩,T) is universal among pairs (B,b∈B_{≤1}), the canonical B⊗̂_A A⟨T⟩ → B⟨T⟩ is isometric, and for every closed ideal J of A⟨T⟩ the canonical morphism B⟨T⟩/JB⟨T⟩⁻ → B⊗̂_A(A⟨T⟩/J) is isometric (2.2).

items.name: Spectral semi-norm, spectral norms, and multiplicativity
items.statement: The spectral semi-norm is |a|_sp := lim_m |a^m|^{1/m}; it need not be a norm. One has |·|_sp ≤ |·|, and |·| is called spectral (equivalently power-multiplicative) when |·|_sp=|·|, in which case A°=A_{≤1} and A°°=A_{<1}. A K-algebra norm is multiplicative iff it is spectral and A°/A°° is a domain. In the complete case |·|_sp is the supremum of the bounded multiplicative semi-norms, i.e. of the points of the Berkovich spectrum ℳ(A).

items.name: Uniform normed algebras
items.statement: A normed K-algebra is uniform if A° is bounded, equivalently if the norm is equivalent to its spectral semi-norm (one inclusion because A° lies in the unit ball of |·|_sp, the other from |a| ≤ |a|_sp·sup_{b∈A°}|b|). Every uniform normed algebra is reduced, and if |K| is dense in R₊ then A°°=K°°A°=(A°°)².

items.name: Reduced affinoids and A⟨T⟩ are uniform
items.statement: Every reduced classical K-affinoid algebra (a quotient of K⟨T₁,…,T_n⟩) is uniform, and for such an algebra the algebraic structure determines both the topology and the spectral norm. If A is uniform (resp. spectral) so is A⟨T⟩, with A⟨T⟩°=A°⟨T⟩ bounded (resp. the unit ball).

items.name: Continuity criterion for uniform algebras
items.statement: A homomorphism φ:A→B of uniform normed K-algebras is continuous iff φ(A°)⊆B°, and, when both norms are spectral, iff ‖φ‖≤1.

items.name: Completion of a uniform algebra; uniform = complete for the spectral semi-norm
items.statement: The completion of a uniform normed algebra is a uniform Banach algebra, and a Banach algebra is uniform iff it is complete for its spectral semi-norm (which is then a norm). Both use the open mapping theorem.

items.name: K-uBan and the uniformization functor
items.statement: K-uBan (resp. A-uBan) is the full subcategory of uniform Banach algebras. The embedding K-uBan ↪ K-Ban has a left adjoint, uniformization A↦A^u, the separated completion for the spectral semi-norm; A^u is spectral and the unit A→A^u is an isomorphism iff A is uniform. K-uBan has initial object K, final object 0 and amalgamated sums B⊗̂^u_A C, hence finite colimits, and uniformization turns ⊗̂ into ⊗̂^u. The uniform analogue (B⟨T⟩/JB⟨T⟩)^u → B⊗̂^u_A(A⟨T⟩/J) of (2.2) is isometric (2.4).

items.name: K-uBan has finite limits; idempotents and factors
items.statement: A finite fibre product of uniform Banach algebras, with the supremum norm, is uniform, so K-uBan has finite limits. Every factor of a uniform Banach algebra is uniform: in a normed algebra a non-zero idempotent has norm ≥1, and norm 1 if the algebra is spectral, and every algebra decomposition A=B×C comes from one in the category of uniform normed algebras.

items.name: Isometry into the uniformized tensor product
items.statement: If C has an orthogonal basis over A and B is spectral, then b↦b⊗1 embeds B isometrically in B⊗̂^u_A C, since |b⊗1|_sp = lim_m|b^m⊗1|^{1/m} = |b|.

items.name: L⊗_K L for a finite Galois extension
items.statement: For L/K finite Galois with group G, carrying the unique extension of the absolute value, L⊗_K L with the tensor-product semi-norm is a finite-dimensional uniform Banach K-algebra, the canonical L⊗_K L → ∏_{γ∈G} L is a continuous bijection hence an isomorphism of Banach algebras, and L⊗̂^u_K L ≅ ∏_G L. The norm of L⊗_K L is spectral iff that map is isometric, which says that L^{oa}/K^{oa} is Galois in the setting (K°,K°°); for a discrete valuation this holds iff L/K is unramified.

items.name: Standing hypothesis: residue characteristic p > 0
items.statement: From the end of §2.2 onwards the residue field k is assumed of characteristic p > 0.

items.name: Integral, almost integral and p-radicial closures
items.statement: For R ⊆ S, an element is integral (resp. almost integral) over R if its powers generate (resp. are contained in) a finite-type R-submodule of S; the corresponding subrings are the integral closure R⁺_S and the complete integral closure R*_S, with R⁺_S ⊆ R*_S and equality for R noetherian. R⁺_S is integrally closed in S but R*_S need not be completely integrally closed. An element is p-radicial over R if some p^n-th power lies in R; the p-radicial closure R†_S is the smallest intermediate ring that is p-radicially closed, the increasing union of R₀=R, R_{i+1}= the subring generated by the p-radicial elements of R_i, and R†_S ⊆ R⁺_S. In characteristic p, or when S=R[1/p], the p-radicial elements already form a subring. All three closures are functorial; integral and p-radicial closure commute with localization, complete integral closure does not.

items.name: The dictionary between norms and flat K°-algebras
items.statement: Fix ϖ∈K°°∖0 and let Γ⊆R be defined by |ϖ|^Γ=|K^×|, with ϖ_s∈K^× of norm |ϖ|^s. For a normed K-algebra with |K| dense in |A| one recovers the norm from the unit ball by |a|=|ϖ|^r with r=sup{s∈Γ : ϖ_{−s}a∈A_{≤1}} (2.5), so the topology of A_{≤1} is ϖ-adic and A is Banach iff A_{≤1} is ϖ-adically complete. Conversely a flat (ϖ-torsion-free) K°-algebra 𝔄 with A:=𝔄[1/ϖ] carries ^𝔄|a| := |ϖ|^r, r=sup{s∈Γ : ϖ_{−s}a∈𝔄} (2.6), a semi-norm, and a norm iff no non-zero element of 𝔄 is infinitely ϖ-divisible.

items.name: Sorite 2.3.1(2b–2e): unit balls, continuity, subalgebras, tensor products
items.statement: With ^𝔄|·| as above: A_{<1}=K°°𝔄 and A_{≤1}=𝔄 when Γ is discrete, A_{≤1}=𝔄_* := Hom_{K°}(K°°,𝔄)=∩_{s>0}ϖ_{−s}𝔄 in general. A homomorphism 𝔄[1/ϖ]→𝔄′[1/ϖ] is continuous if it carries 𝔄 into 𝔄′, and isometric if moreover the preimage of 𝔄′ is 𝔄; a continuous φ is isometric iff φ(A_{≤1})⊆A′_{≤1} and A_{≤1}/ϖ → A′_{≤1}/ϖ is injective. Sub-objects and quotients with ϖ-torsion-free cokernel induce the expected semi-norms, and (A/ℐ)_{≤1}=(A_{≤1}/ℐ_{≤1})_*. For tensor products, the semi-norm of (𝔅⊗_𝔄ℭ)/(ϖ^∞-torsion) is the tensor-product semi-norm, and dually (B⊗_A C)_{≤1} is (B_{≤1}⊗_{A_{≤1}}C_{≤1})/(ϖ^∞-tors), with (·)_* applied when Γ is not discrete; similarly for completed tensor products.

items.name: Sorite 2.3.1(3): integrally closed open subalgebras
items.statement: Reduction modulo A°° (resp. completion) is a bijection between the open K°-subalgebras [completely] integrally closed in A° and the [completely] integrally closed k-subalgebras of A°/A°° (resp. the open K°-subalgebras integrally closed in Â°). The proof isolates a lemma of independent use: for I ⊆ R ⊆ S with I an ideal of S, an element of S is integral over R iff its image is integral over R/I, and likewise for complete integrality.

items.name: Sorite 2.3.1(4): the chain of closures and the spectral unit ball
items.statement: Writing 𝔄†_A={a : a^{p^n}∈𝔄 for some n} and 𝔄*_A={a : ∃m ∀n, ϖ^m a^n∈𝔄}, one has (2.7) 𝔄†_A ⊆ 𝔄⁺_A ⊆ 𝔄*_A = (𝔄_*)*_A = A°, and (𝔄†_A)_*=(A°)_* is the unit ball of the spectral semi-norm. In particular if A_{≤1} is noetherian its integral closure in A is A°. The proof is Fekete subadditivity: inf_n |a^{p^n}|^{1/p^n} = lim_n |a^{p^n}|^{1/p^n} = |a|_sp.

items.name: Sorite 2.3.1(5)–(7): six characterizations of spectrality
items.statement: The following are equivalent: the norm is spectral; A_{≤1}=A°; A_{≤1} is completely integrally closed in A; A_{≤1} is integrally closed in A; A_{≤1} is p-radicially closed in A; and (when |ϖ|≥|p| and 1/p∈Γ) x↦x^p is injective A_{≤1}/ϖ_{1/p} → A_{≤1}/ϖ. If A is uniform then A°=(A°)_*=(A_{≤1})*_A and (A°)^ = (Â)° (2.8). If A is Banach, A^{uo} is the separated completion of (A°)_* for the spectral semi-norm.

items.name: The inclusions of (2.7) can be strict
items.statement: Frobenius A°/ϖ_{1/p} → A°/ϖ is injective even without uniformity. The inclusions 𝔄⁺_A ⊆ 𝔄*_A = A° ⊆ A_{|·|_sp≤1} may be strict: for 𝔄=K°[ϖT,…,ϖ^{i+1}T^{p^i},…] ⊆ K°[T] one has |T^m|=|ϖ|^{−1−[log_p m]}, A=K[T], A°=𝔄*_A=K°+K°°TK°[T] and 𝔄**_A=K°[T]. This gives a complete integral closure that is not completely integrally closed, and an A° that is not the unit ball of the spectral norm.

items.name: Uniform Banach algebras ≅ K°-algebras with four conditions
items.statement: Assume |K| dense in R₊. The functor B↦B° is an equivalence from uniform Banach K-algebras onto the K°-algebras 𝔅 that are (1) flat over K°, (2) ϖ-adically complete, (3) [p-radicially / integrally / completely integrally] closed in 𝔅[1/ϖ] and (4) equal to Hom_{K°}(K°°,𝔅); a quasi-inverse is 𝔅↦(𝔅[1/ϖ], ^𝔅|·|). Under (4) the three readings of (3) agree, and say exactly that ^𝔅|·| is spectral. The same holds over a base A.

items.name: Idempotents are detected on the unit ball and its reductions
items.statement: For B a uniform Banach K-algebra the idempotents of B, of B°, of B°/ϖ and of B°/B°° correspond bijectively.

items.name: The almost-elements endofunctor preserves the four conditions
items.statement: Let A be a uniform Banach K-algebra and 𝔪 an idempotent ideal of A° with K°°𝔪=𝔪. The endofunctor 𝔅 ↦ (𝔅^a)_* = Hom_{A°}(𝔪̃,𝔅) on A°-algebras respects each of conditions (1)–(4) of Corollaire 2.3.2 (2.9); hence on that subcategory the almost-elements functor is right adjoint to (·)^a and commutes with limits. The passage from (K°,K°°) to (A°,𝔪) goes through (A°,K°°A°=A°°), the meaning of "almost" being unchanged.

items.name: The corrected left adjoint (·)^!!
items.statement: The left adjoint (·)_!! of (·)^a does not respect conditions (2)–(4), but can be corrected to a left adjoint (·)^!! on the category of A°-algebras satisfying (1)–(4), by quotienting 𝔅_!! by ϖ-primary torsion, completing, passing to the [p-radicial/integral] closure in the 1/ϖ-localization and taking almost elements; each step is a reflector and by Sorite 2.3.1(4) they do not undo one another, the last two amounting to taking power-bounded elements in the localization. The coproduct of that category is not ⊗ but the completion of the complete integral closure of (𝔅⊗_𝔄ℭ)/(ϖ^∞-tors) in (𝔅⊗_𝔄ℭ)[1/ϖ].

items.name: The almost category A^â-uBan and its adjunction (2.10)
items.statement: Almost algebra does not extend naively to topological modules, since topological modules and continuous homomorphisms do not form an abelian category. For a fixed uniform Banach K-algebra A, the category A^â-uBan has as objects the uniform A-Banach algebras, written B^â, with Hom(B^â,C^â) := Hom(B^{oa},C^{oa}) in the setting (A°,𝔪); for the setting (K°,K°°) it is isomorphic to K-uBan. The functor (·)^â is the identity on objects and, by Lemme 2.3.4, has a right adjoint (·)^_* with unit B → (B^â)^_* = (B^{oa})_*[1/ϖ] = Hom_{A°}(𝔪̃,B°)[1/ϖ] = Hom^cont_A(𝔪̃⊗A,B) (2.10), injective when 𝔪 acts faithfully, with ((B^â)^_*)° = Hom_{A°}(𝔪̃,B°); it also has a left adjoint (·)^!!. The inclusion (B^â)^_* ⊆ (B^a)_* = Hom_{A°}(𝔪̃,B) is not an equality in general.

items.name: Almost isomorphism is detected on the unit ball
items.statement: A morphism φ:B→C of uniform A-Banach algebras is an almost isomorphism in the setting (A°,𝔪) iff its restriction φ°:B°→C° is, i.e. iff φ^â is an isomorphism.

items.name: A ∩ B° = A° for a normed extension
items.statement: If A is a uniform normed K-algebra and B an extension carrying a norm extending that of A, then A∩B°=A°.

items.name: Lemme 2.4.1(1): the complete integral closure of A° lies in B°
items.statement: The complete integral closure of A° in B is contained in B°; in particular A° is completely integrally closed in A. (A finite-type A°-submodule of B containing all powers of b is bounded, because A° is bounded and A→B is continuous.)

items.name: Lemme 2.4.1(2): invariants under a finite group and integrality
items.statement: Let a finite group G act on B with B^G=A, and suppose G preserves the norm. Then B^{oG}=A°, B is integral over A, B° is integral over A°, and B° is the integral closure of A° in B. The hypothesis holds in particular when the norm is spectral and complete — but the paper justifies that by the uniqueness of a complete spectral norm, which is false as stated; see source issue E1. What repairs it is the papers own part (3): γ(b) satisfies the same monic polynomial ∏_{γ∈G}(T−γ(b))∈A[T] as b, whose coefficients determine the spectral value by [6, 3.1.2 prop. 1].
items.note: Statement recorded in its corrected form: the G-invariance of the spectral norm is derived from the characteristic polynomial, not from uniqueness of the complete spectral norm (E1, E10).

items.name: Lemme 2.4.1(3)–(4): the unique G-invariant spectral norm
items.statement: If in addition B is uniform, |·|_sp is the unique G-invariant spectral norm on B extending that of A: for b∈B the polynomial ∏_{γ∈G}(T−γ(b))=T^d+Σa_iT^{d−i}∈A[T] gives max_γ|γ(b)|′ = max_i|a_i|^{1/i} (2.11) for any such norm |·|′, whence equality with |·|_sp by G-invariance. If moreover the norm of B is spectral and g∈A, then multiplication by g in B is injective (resp. isometric) as soon as multiplication by g in A is, since replacing b by ab replaces a_i by a^i a_i.

items.name: Sharpness of Lemme 2.4.1: three prophylactic examples
items.statement: Without norm-invariance, B° need not be integral over A°: for V a complete discrete valuation ring of residue characteristic ≠2, A=V[[T]][1/ϖ] and B=A[U]/(U²−TU+ϖ)=A[√(T²−4ϖ)], the polynomial is irreducible over Q(A) but splits in the completion of A[1/T], so B carries two multiplicative norms extending that of A; for the second (neither G-invariant nor complete) the element U/ϖ=1/(T−U) has norm 1 and is not integral over A. Under the hypothesis of (2), B need not be finite over A: in characteristic 2 with A=(K°[[T^{1/2^∞}]])^[1/ϖ] and B the radicial closure of A[U]/(U²−TU−1), B/A = (U/T)·T^{1/2^∞}A is not of finite type. Even for B finite and split over A, B° need not be finite over A° and A°→B° need not split: take A=K and B=K[U]/(U²−ϖU−1).

items.name: Forgetting the norm is fully faithful on finite étale algebras
items.statement: For A a uniform Banach K-algebra, the functor {finite étale uniform Banach A-algebras} → {finite étale A-algebras} that forgets the norm is fully faithful; a quotient of a finite étale A-algebra is a direct factor, which reduces fullness to isomorphisms, and those are isometric by uniqueness of the complete spectral norm. It is in fact an equivalence ([21, prop. 2.8.16(b)]), a fact the paper does not use.

items.name: Monomorphisms and free objects in K-uBan
items.statement: The monomorphisms of K-uBan are exactly the injective continuous homomorphisms. K-uBan has free objects, S ↦ K⟨T_s⟩_{s∈S} being left adjoint to the forgetful functor to sets, with Hom(K⟨T⟩,B)=B°.

items.name: The setting (K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, T^{1/p^∞}K°°) and compatible p-power roots
items.statement: Assume |K| dense in R₊. The setting fundamental for the sequel is the passage from (K°,K°°) to 𝔙=K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩=(K°[T^{1/p^∞}])^ with 𝔪=T^{1/p^∞}𝔙^{oo}=(T)^{1/p^∞}K°°𝔙; one has K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩°=K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and 𝔪 is flat, so 𝔪=𝔪̃. A morphism K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩→B to a uniform Banach K-algebra is the same as a compatible system (g^{1/p^m}) of p^m-th roots of an element g∈B°.

items.name: The almost elements are the root saturation g^{−1/p^∞}B°
items.statement: Let B be a uniform Banach K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra and g the image of T. The canonical (B^{oa})_* → B°[1/g] is injective with image the ϖ-adically complete ring g^{−1/p^∞}B° := ∩_m g^{−1/p^m}B° (2.12)–(2.14); B° → (B^{oa})_* is injective iff g is not a zero divisor; and (B^{oa})_*/ϖ → (B^{oa}/ϖ)_* is injective. The proof uses uniformity through Sorite 2.3.1(6) and the presentation of 𝔪 as a colimit along multiplication by T^{1/p^m−1/p^{m+1}}.

items.name: Nothing is gained when g is invertible
items.statement: If g is invertible in B then B°=g^{−1/p^∞}B°.

items.name: The norm on the root saturation and the identification with B^â_*
items.statement: For b∈g^{−1/p^∞}B put |b| := sup_m |g^{1/p^m}b|_B ∈ R∪{+∞} (2.15); it has all the properties of a norm except finiteness, the elements of finite norm form a uniform Banach algebra (spectral if B is), and its associated spectral algebra is B^â_* of §2.3.6, because (g^{−1/p^∞}B)° = g^{−1/p^∞}B° (2.16).

items.name: The isometric case, and the failure of (2.17) without it
items.statement: If multiplication by g is isometric then B°[1/g]∩B=B°, the ideals g^{1/p^m}B° are closed, B° ↪ g^{−1/p^∞}B° is isometric, (2.15) is a norm making g^{−1/p^∞}B a uniform Banach algebra, and g^{−1/p^∞}B = g^{−1/p^∞}B°[1/ϖ] = B_* in the setting (K°[T^{1/p^∞}],(T)^{1/p^∞}K°°K°[T^{1/p^∞}]) (2.17). The inclusion B° ⊆ g^{−1/p^∞}B° is in general strict even then, as the completion of K+T₁^{1/p^∞}K⟨T₁^{1/p^∞},T₂^{1/p^∞}⟩ with g=T₁ shows. Without isometry, even for g a non-zero-divisor, B° ↪ g^{−1/p^∞}B° need not be isometric and g^{−1/p^∞}B°[1/ϖ] may differ from g^{−1/p^∞}B: for K perfect of characteristic p, the perfect K°-algebra K°⟨T₁^{1/p^∞},(ϖ^mT₁^{1/p^m}T₂)^{1/p^∞}⟩_m is B° for a uniform Banach K⟨T₁^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra with B=T₁^{−1/p^∞}B°[1/ϖ] ≠ T₁^{−1/p^∞}B ∋ T₂.
items.note: Formula (2.17) is printed with [1/p] where [1/ϖ] is meant; recorded in its corrected form (source issue E5).

items.name: Explicit complete integral closures and their invariants
items.statement: For g a non-zero-divisor, the complete integral closure of B° in B°[1/g] is {b : ∃m ∀n, g^m b^n ∈ B°} (2.18) and in B[1/g]=B°[1/ϖg] it is {b : ∃m ∀n, (ϖg)^m b^n ∈ B°} (2.19); and for a group G of automorphisms of B° fixing g, (B^{o*}_{B[1/g]})^G = B^{oG*}_{B^G[1/g]} (2.20).

items.name: Six equivalent closedness conditions for the root saturation
items.statement: For B a uniform Banach (or merely uniform normed) K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra with g the image of T a non-zero-divisor, the following are equivalent: g^{−1/p^∞}B° is p-radicially closed in B°[1/g]; it is p-radicially closed in B[1/g]; it equals (B°)*_{B°[1/g]}; it equals (B°)*_{B[1/g]}; it is completely integrally closed in B°[1/g]; it is completely integrally closed in B[1/g]. The proof runs along g^{−1/p^∞}B° ⊆ B^{o*}_{B°[1/g]} ⊆ B^{o*}_{B[1/g]} ⊆ (g^{−1/p^∞}B°)*_{B[1/g]}. This is what makes the terminology "almost integral" consonate with almost algebra.

items.name: Complete integral closure as a root saturation of the p-radicial closure
items.statement: For any ring R containing a compatible system t^{1/p^m} of roots of a non-zero-divisor t, R*_{R[1/t]} = t^{−1/p^∞}R†_{R[1/t]}.

items.name: Epimorphisms and extremal epimorphisms in K-uBan
items.statement: In K-uBan every morphism with dense image is an epimorphism. An epimorphism φ is extremal if in every factorisation φ=μ∘λ with μ a monomorphism, μ is an isomorphism. Every morphism A→B factors canonically as A→(A/ker φ)^u→B with the first map an extremal epimorphism; it is not clear that the second is a monomorphism, so it is not clear that every extremal epimorphism has this form. Every surjective morphism is extremal, the target norm then being equivalent to the quotient semi-norm by the open mapping theorem.

items.name: Uniform rational localization A{f₁,…,f_n/f}
items.statement: For f₁,…,f_n,f generating the unit ideal, A{f₁,…,f_n/f} := A⟨U₁,…,U_n⟩/(fU_i−f_i)⁻_i (2.21) is the universal Banach A-algebra in which f becomes invertible and the f_i/f are power-bounded; A→A{f₁,…,f_n/f} is an epimorphism because A[1/f]→A{…} has dense image. For n=1, f₁=1 one writes A{1/f} := A⟨U⟩/(fU−1)⁻ (2.22), universal for f invertible with inverse in the unit ball; A{1/f}=0 when f∈A°°. The reference [6, 6.1.4] assumes A affinoid, so that the ideal is closed; substituting its closure, the arguments hold for an arbitrary Banach K-algebra.

items.name: For uniform A the ideal (fU−1) is closed
items.statement: If A is uniform, the ideal (fU−1) of A⟨U⟩ is closed, so the closure in (2.22) is superfluous.

items.name: The localization A{λ/g} as a K⟨T⟩-algebra, and its elementary calculus
items.statement: Fix λ∈K° with g:=λf∈A° and regard A{λ/g} := A{1/f} (2.23) as a Banach K⟨T⟩-algebra by T↦g, with canonical ι_{λ/g}:A→A{λ/g}. Then A{λ/g} ≅ A⊗̂_{K⟨T⟩}K⟨T⟩{λ/T} isometrically (2.24), and A{λ/g}=0 if g∈λA°°. For |λ|≤|μ| there is a canonical A{λ/g}→A{μ/g} and A{μ/g} ≅ A{λ/g}{μ/g}; if |g−h|<|λ| then A{λ/g} ≅ A{λ/h}; and |ι_{λ/g}(a)| = inf_m |(g/λ)^m a|_A.

items.name: Closed-annulus examples; isomorphic but not isometric
items.statement: For the spectral algebra A=K⟨T⟩, K⟨T,λ/T⟩ := A{λ/T} is the spectral algebra of the closed annulus of radii (|λ|,1), with unit ball K°⟨T,λ/T⟩; its norm is multiplicative only if λ=0 or |λ|=1. The Banach algebras K⟨T,λ/T⟩ and K⟨T,λ²/T²⟩ are isomorphic but not isometric, the first being spectral and the second not. For A multiplicatively normed, A{1/g}=A{1/g}^u is a Banach subalgebra of the completion of the fraction field of A.

items.name: A{λ/g} need not be uniform; the uniform localization is a left adjoint
items.statement: A{λ/g} can fail to be uniform, though not for A a reduced affinoid with its spectral norm. In every case A→A{λ/g}^u is an epimorphism of K-uBan, since the image of A[1/g] is dense. The functor A ↦ A{λ/(T·1)}^u is left adjoint to the inclusion into K⟨T⟩-uBan of the full subcategory of those B in which (T·1)/λ is invertible with inverse in B°.

items.name: Invariance of A{λ/g} under an intermediate Banach algebra
items.statement: Let g∈A be a non-zero-divisor and A ↪ A′ a monomorphism of Banach algebras with A′ contained in A[1/g] as an A-algebra. Then A{λ/g} → A′{λ/g} is an isomorphism of Banach algebras. (Proof due to O. Gabber, by Baire and the open mapping theorem applied to ⊕̂_m V_m ↠ A′ with V_n ⊆ A′×A the closed subspace of pairs (a′, g^n a′).)

items.name: A° injects into the limit of the localizations
items.statement: For A uniform and g a non-zero-divisor, A° → lim_{λ→0} A{λ/g}° is injective. The printed proof asserts inf_m|(g/λ)^m a| ≥ 1 when |λ| ≤ |ga|, which is false; what holds, and suffices, is inf_m|(g/λ)^m a| ≥ |a| > 0 (see source issue E6).
items.note: Statement recorded with the corrected bound of E6; the lemma itself is unaffected.

items.name: When ι_{λ/g} is injective
items.statement: ι_{λ/g} is injective iff (inf_m |(g/λ)^m a|_A = 0 ⇒ a = 0), which holds when multiplication by g in A is isometric. The morphisms A{λ/g}^u → A{μ/g}^u are always injective, although multiplication by g in A{λ/g}° is not isometric for |λ|<1. Injectivity can fail for A uniform without g-torsion: the completion of K°[T₁,T₂,T₂T₁^i/ϖ^i]_{i≥1} is the unit ball of such an A, and ι_{λ/T₁}(T₂)=0 whenever |λ|>|ϖ|.

items.name: Uniform products exist in K-uBan
items.statement: Infinite products of Banach algebras do not exist in general: for A non-uniform and (a_n) an unbounded sequence in A°, the family of morphisms K⟨T⟩ → A, T↦a_n, cannot be equivalent to a single morphism to a Banach algebra. By contrast, morphisms of spectrally normed algebras satisfy ‖φ‖≤1, so K-uBan has arbitrary products: ∏^u A^α := {(a^α) : sup|a^α|_sp < ∞} (2.25), with (∏^u A^α)° = ∏ A^{αo}, the empty product being 0.
items.note: The printed source of the test morphisms is K rather than the free object K⟨T⟩; recorded in corrected form (source issue E8).

items.name: Decomposition into connected factors, and its failure
items.statement: A spectral Banach K-algebra decomposes as a uniform product of connected factors, equivalently A°=∏A^{αo}, if and only if its Boolean algebra of idempotents B(A) is complete and atomic. Conversely every Boolean algebra B is realised: the uniform Banach algebra A := (K⟨T_b⟩_{b∈B}/(T_bT_{b′}−T_{b∧b′}, T_b+T_{¬b}−1))^u topologically generated by idempotents has B(A) ≅ B, so for B free infinite — never complete nor atomic — A admits no such decomposition. Moreover ℳ(A) is then the maximal spectrum of B, the profinite space of connected components of Spec A, and A the algebra of bounded continuous K-valued functions on it. A uniform Banach algebra is connected iff ℳ(A) is connected.
items.note: The second relation is printed T_b+T_{¬b′}−1, which collapses the construction; recorded in corrected form (source issue E7).

items.name: The Gelfand transform
items.statement: The Gelfand transform of a uniform Banach K-algebra is ΓA := ∏^u_{x∈ℳ(A)} ℋ(x) (2.26), the uniform product over the points of the Berkovich spectrum of the completed residue fields. The canonical A→ΓA is a monomorphism, isometric iff A is spectral, and ℳ(ΓA) is the Stone–Čech compactification of ℳ(A) made discrete, mapping onto ℳ(A). Γ is a faithful, non-full endofunctor of K-uBan, and a continuous homomorphism of spectral Banach algebras is isometric as soon as the induced ℳ(B)→ℳ(A) is surjective.

items.name: K-uBan is complete; uniform limits
items.statement: K-uBan has equalizers, represented by closed subalgebras, and products, hence all small limits. For a projective system (A^α), not necessarily filtered, the limit is the uniform limit ulim A^α := {(a^α)∈lim A^α : sup|a^α|_sp < ∞} (2.27), a spectral Banach algebra with (ulim A^α)° = lim A^{αo} (2.28); conditions (1)–(4) of Corollaire 2.3.2 pass to the limit.

items.name: Open unit disc and the simplest Riemann extension
items.statement: For (r_i) increasing to 1, the algebras of analytic functions on the closed discs of radius r_i have uniform limit K°[[T]]⊗_{K°}K, the bounded analytic functions on the open unit disc. For |ϖ|<1 the closed-annulus algebras K⟨T,ϖ^j/T⟩ have uniform limit K⟨T⟩ — the simplest case of the non-archimedean Riemann extension theorem of §4.

items.name: Injectivity of A°/ϖ into the limit of the reductions
items.statement: For a projective system of uniform Banach K-algebras with uniform limit A, the canonical A°/ϖ → lim(A^{αo}/ϖ) is injective, because each A^{αo} is ϖ-torsion-free.

items.name: Root saturation commutes with projective limits
items.statement: For a projective system of uniform Banach K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebras, the uniform limit is again one, and g^{−1/p^∞} lim A^{αo} ≅ lim g^{−1/p^∞}A^{αo}. Applied to the system of localizations A{ϖ^j/g}^u, which contain 1/g, this shows that the uniform limit Ã satisfies Ã° = g^{−1/p^∞}Ã°.

items.name: Uniform filtered colimits
items.statement: For a filtered inductive system (B_α), equip colim B_α with the limit semi-norm |(b_α)| = lim_α |b_α|_sp and define ucolim B_α as its separated completion: a spectral Banach algebra, and a filtered colimit in K-uBan, with (ucolim B_α)° = (colim B^o_α)^_*. If the norms are spectral and the transition maps isometric, each B_β → ucolim B_α is isometric and (ucolim B_α)° = (colim B^o_α)^.

items.name: K-uBan is cocomplete
items.statement: Having filtered colimits, pushouts ⊗̂^u and an initial object, K-uBan has all small colimits.

items.name: Uniform colimits commute with uniform localization
items.statement: ucolim commutes with ⊗̂^u, hence with the uniform localization (·){λ/g}^u by (2.24); equivalently, because uniform localization is a left adjoint.

items.name: The algebras A⟨g^{1/p^i}⟩ and A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩
items.statement: For A a spectral Banach K-algebra and g∈A°, viewed as a K⟨T⟩-algebra by T↦g, set A⟨g^{1/p^i}⟩ := A⊗̂^u_{K⟨T⟩}K⟨T^{1/p^i}⟩ and A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ := ucolim_i A⟨g^{1/p^i}⟩ = A⊗̂^u_{K⟨T⟩}K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (2.29). Since K⟨T^{1/p^{i+1}}⟩ has the orthogonal basis 1,T^{1/p^{i+1}},…,T^{(p−1)/p^{i+1}} over K⟨T^{1/p^i}⟩, all the transition maps and A → A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ are isometric, and A⟨g^{1/p^i}⟩ = (A⟨T^{1/p^i}⟩/(T−g))^u (2.30). In characteristic p, ucolim K^{1/p^i} is the completed perfect closure of K.

items.name: Every uniform Banach algebra is a filtered colimit of reduced affinoids
items.statement: Every uniform Banach K-algebra B is a filtered uniform colimit of reduced affinoid K-algebras B_α with colim B_α → B bijective: take for B_α the image in B of the free object on a finite subset α ⊆ B°. Reduced affinoids are nevertheless not finitely presented in the categorical sense in K-uBan, since Hom(K⟨T⟩, ucolim B_α) = (colim B^o_α)^_* while colim Hom(K⟨T⟩,B_α) = colim B^o_α.

items.name: The uniform colimit of shrinking discs is K
items.statement: The algebras K⟨T/ϖ^i⟩ of analytic functions on the closed discs of radius |ϖ|^i form an inductive system whose ordinary colimit is the germs of analytic functions at the origin; the limit semi-norm is |Σa_jT^j| = lim_i max_j |a_jϖ^{ij}| = |a_0|, so the uniform colimit is K, the maps being evaluation at 0.

items.name: The uniform colimit of tubular neighbourhoods
items.statement: For B a uniform Banach K-algebra and f∈B° there is a canonical isomorphism ucolim_i B{f/ϖ^i}^u ≅ (B/fB)^u (2.31).

items.name: The root algebra as a uniform colimit of localizations
items.statement: For A a uniform Banach K-algebra and g∈A°, ucolim_i A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{(T−g)/ϖ^i}^u ≅ A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩, and correspondingly on unit balls ((colim_i A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{(T−g)/ϖ^i}°)^)_* ≅ A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩° (2.32).

items.name: Perfectoid fields: three equivalent conditions
items.statement: K complete for a non-archimedean non-discrete absolute value with residue field k of characteristic p is perfectoid if Frobenius is surjective on K°/p; equivalently on K°/ϖ for every ϖ∈K°°∖0 with pK°⊆ϖK°; equivalently x↦x^p is bijective K°/ϖ_{1/p} → K°/ϖ for every ϖ_{1/p} of norm |ϖ|^{1/p}. Then the topology of K° is ϖ-adic, the value group is p-divisible hence dense, and k is perfect; a perfectoid field of characteristic p is perfect.

items.name: Perfectoid = deeply ramified
items.statement: K complete for a non-archimedean non-discrete absolute value is a perfectoid field if and only if it is deeply ramified, i.e. Ω_{(K^s)°/K°} is annihilated by K°°.

items.name: The cyclotomic and Kummer perfectoid fields
items.statement: For k perfect and K₀=Frac W(k), fix a compatible system (ζ_{p^i}) of primitive p^i-th roots of unity and put K_i=K₀(ζ_{p^i}); then K_i°=W(k)[ζ_{p^i}] with uniformizer ζ_{p^i}−1 and K_i° ≡ (K_{i+1}°)^p mod p, so the completion K̂_∞ of ∪K_i is a perfectoid field with value group (1/(p−1))Z[1/p]. Likewise the completion of K₀(π^{1/p^∞}) is perfectoid for π a uniformizer. The completion of any algebraic extension of a perfectoid field is perfectoid.

items.name: Perfectoid K-algebras: five equivalent conditions
items.statement: A uniform Banach algebra A over a perfectoid field K is perfectoid if Frobenius is surjective on A°/p; equivalently almost surjective in the setting (K°,K°°); equivalently surjective on A°/ϖ; equivalently x↦x^p is bijective A°/ϖ_{1/p} → A°/ϖ; equivalently Frobenius induces an isomorphism (resp. almost isomorphism) A°/ϖ_{1/p} ⊗_{K°/ϖ_{1/p},σ} K°/ϖ ≅ A°/ϖ. Morphisms are the continuous algebra homomorphisms, so K-Perf is a full subcategory of K-uBan with initial object K and final object 0; over a fixed Banach algebra A one has the category A-Perf.

items.name: In characteristic p, perfectoid = perfect and uniformity is automatic
items.statement: If char K = p, a uniform Banach K-algebra is perfectoid iff it is perfect. Moreover a Banach K-algebra is uniform iff it is reduced with A^p closed, i.e. iff Frobenius is injective with closed image; hence a Banach K-algebra is perfectoid iff it is perfect, uniformity being automatic. A multiplicatively normed perfectoid algebra has perfectoid fraction-field completion. André records that the necessary hypothesis "reduced" is omitted from the statement of [18, lem. 3.5] though used in its proof.
items.note: Footnote 16 is itself an erratum against [18], recorded here as part of the statement.

items.name: Adjoints of K-Perf ⊆ K-uBan in characteristic p
items.statement: For char K = p, the inclusion of perfectoid into uniform Banach K-algebras has left adjoint A ↦ ucolim_F A, the completed radicial closure, and right adjoint A ↦ ulim_F A.

items.name: Perfectoid algebras as integral objects
items.statement: The functor A ↦ A° is an equivalence from perfectoid K-algebras onto the K°-algebras 𝔄 that are flat, complete, satisfy 𝔄=𝔄_*, and for which 𝔄/ϖ_{1/p} → 𝔄/ϖ, x↦x^p, is bijective; in characteristic p this reads: perfect, flat, complete and 𝔄=𝔄_*. The only extra point beyond Corollaire 2.3.2 is that 𝔄[1/ϖ] is then uniform, by Sorite 2.3.1(5f).

items.name: K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, its universal property, and the Witt description of Â_∞
items.statement: K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = ucolim_i K[T^{1/p^i}] is perfectoid with unit ball K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, and more generally A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid for A perfectoid; the pair (A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩,(T^{1/p^∞})) is universal among pairs (B,(g^{1/p^∞})) with B an A-perfectoid algebra and (g^{1/p^∞}) a compatible system of p^m-th roots of an element of B°. With A_i := K_i°[[T_1^{1/p^i},…,T_n^{1/p^i}]]⊗_{K_i°}K_i, each A_i° is a complete regular noetherian local ring of dimension n+1 with A_i° ≡ (A_{i+1}°)^p mod p, so Â_∞ = ucolim A_i is a perfectoid K̂_∞-algebra; its unit ball is strictly contained in K̂_∞°[[T^{1/p^∞}]]^ and satisfies Â_∞° ≅ W(k[[T_1^{1/p^∞},…,T_n^{1/p^∞}]])^ ⊗̂_{W(k)} K̂_∞° (3.1).

items.name: The tilt of a perfectoid field
items.statement: For char K = 0, the multiplicative bijection lim_{x↦x^p}K° → lim_F K°/ϖ gives a continuous multiplicative # : lim_F K°/ϖ → K°; there is ϖ♭ with |#(ϖ♭)|=|ϖ|, K♭° := lim_F K°/ϖ is the valuation ring of the perfectoid field K♭ := (lim_F K°/ϖ)[1/ϖ♭] of characteristic p with |x♭| := |#(x♭)| (3.2), and # induces K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ.

items.name: The tilting functor on uniform Banach algebras
items.statement: For A a uniform Banach K-algebra the multiplicative lim_{x↦x^p}A° → lim_F A°/ϖ is a homeomorphism, giving # : lim_F A°/ϖ → A° (3.3); lim_F A°/ϖ is a perfect ϖ♭-adically complete K♭°-algebra with |a♭| := |#(a♭)| (3.4), and A♭ := (lim_F A°/ϖ)[1/ϖ♭] (3.5) is a perfectoid Banach K♭-algebra with A♭° = lim_F A°/ϖ, yielding a functor ♭ : K-uBan → K♭-Perf (3.6). Since A is uniform the kernel of F^n on A°/ϖ is ϖ^{1/p^n}(A°/ϖ), so the kernel of lim_F(A°/ϖ) → A°/ϖ is ϖ♭·lim_F(A°/ϖ).

items.name: The tilt is perfectoid, and detects perfectoidness
items.statement: A♭ is perfectoid and # induces an injection A♭°/ϖ♭ ↪ A°/ϖ (3.7), which is an isomorphism if and only if A is perfectoid.

items.name: Tilts of the standard examples
items.statement: K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩♭ ≅ K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, the two elements T corresponding under #. With ϖ♭ := (ζ_{p^i})−1, K̂_∞♭° is the ϖ♭-adic completion of the radicial closure of k[[ϖ♭]] and Â_∞♭° that of k[[ϖ♭,T_1,…,T_n]], the T_i corresponding under #.

items.name: Density, domains, multiplicativity, idempotents and isometries under tilting
items.statement: For A perfectoid, #(A♭°) generates a dense K°-subalgebra of A° (by Nakayama for complete modules). If A is a domain so is A♭; if the norm of A is multiplicative so is that of A♭, and conversely for A perfectoid. Idempotents of A, of A°/ϖ and of A♭ correspond. A morphism of perfectoid algebras is isometric iff its tilt is, the condition being injectivity of φ° mod ϖ, identified with φ♭° mod ϖ♭.

items.name: The tilting equivalence
items.statement: Tilting A ↦ A♭ is an equivalence between perfectoid K-algebras and perfectoid K♭-algebras, independent of the choice of (ϖ,ϖ♭); and passing to (·)° followed by reduction mod ϖ (resp. ϖ♭) identifies each of them with the category of flat K°^a/ϖ-algebras 𝔄̄ whose Frobenius induces 𝔄̄/ϖ_{1/p} ⊗_{K°/ϖ_{1/p},σ} K°/ϖ ≅ 𝔄̄.

items.name: Fontaine’s untilting functor ♯
items.statement: Following Fontaine, K° is a quotient of W(K♭°) and (A♭)^{♯o} := W(A♭°)⊗_{W(K♭°)}K°, (A♭)^♯ := (A♭)^{♯o}[1/ϖ] (3.8) define a functor ♯ : K♭-Perf → K-Perf quasi-inverse to ♭; likewise 𝔄̄ ↦ (lim_F 𝔄̄)^{♯o}, resp. lim_F 𝔄̄, is quasi-inverse to reduction (3.9). For A perfectoid fixed, tilting is an equivalence between A-perfectoid and A♭-perfectoid algebras.

items.name: K-Perf is a coreflective subcategory of K-uBan
items.statement: Setting ♮ := ♯∘♭ : K-uBan → K-Perf (3.10), the functor ♮ is right adjoint to the inclusion ι, the counit A♮ → A is isometric for the spectral norms and is an isomorphism iff A is perfectoid; and ♭ is right adjoint to ι∘♯. In categorical language K-Perf is a full coreflective subcategory of K-uBan.

items.name: Completed tensor products of perfectoid algebras
items.statement: For A perfectoid and B,C two A-perfectoid algebras, the amalgamated sum in K-Perf exists and coincides with B⊗̂^u_A C, and (B°⊗̂_{A°}C°)_* ≅ (B⊗̂_A C)° (3.11); for spectral norms B⊗̂_A C = B⊗̂^u_A C with unit ball (B°⊗̂_{A°}C°)_*. The proof reduces by Lemme 3.2.2 to almost absence of ϖ-torsion, which follows from perfectness in characteristic p and by tilting in characteristic 0; the same argument shows that amalgamated sums commute with tilting. Consequently K-Perf has finite colimits, computed as in K-uBan and commuting with tilting, and −⊗̂_K A is left adjoint to the forgetful functor A-Perf → K-Perf.
items.locator: Proposition 3.3.4 with its corollaries, formula (3.11), pp. 40–41

items.name: Almost purity for perfectoid algebras
items.statement: For K a perfectoid field and A a perfectoid K-algebra there are equivalences {finite étale A°^a-algebras} ≅ {finite étale perfectoid A-algebras} ≅ {finite étale A-algebras}, induced by inverting ϖ and by forgetting the norm, compatible with tilting. In particular every finite étale extension B of A is perfectoid — its spectral norm being the unique spectral norm compatible with the canonical topology of the finite projective A-module B — and every K-automorphism of B fixing A is continuous, hence isometric for the spectral norms. This is the theorem the paper generalises to the ramified case in Théorème 5.2.1.
items.note: The paper also justifies the perfectoidness of B by "l’unique norme spectrale complète", which is the assertion source issue E1 refutes; the alternative justification given in the same parenthesis, uniqueness of the spectral norm compatible with the module topology, is valid and is the one recorded here. The cross-reference printed "cf. 2.2.2" belongs to numbered paragraph 2.2.4 (E2).

items.name: The étale hypothesis cannot be dropped
items.statement: With p=2, n=1 and g := T+4, the multiplicatively normed Banach K̂_∞-algebra Â_∞[√g] is not perfectoid: every a₁+a₂√g in its unit ball satisfies 2a₁,2a₂,a₁²−a₂²g ∈ Â_∞°, so a₁(0)∈K°; the element f := ((i+1)/2)(√(T+4)−√T) lies in the unit ball but has no square root modulo 2, since e=a₁+a₂√g with e²−f ∈ 2Â_∞[√g]° forces 2a₁a₂−(i+1)/2 ∈ Â_∞°, whence |a₁(0)a₂(0)| = 2^{3/2}, contradicting a₁(0), 2a₂(0) ∈ K°.
items.note: Recorded with the corrected exponent: the paper prints 2^{−3/2}, which is compatible with a₁(0), 2a₂(0) ∈ K° and yields no contradiction (source issue E4).

items.name: The integral half of almost purity, proved by Galois descent
items.statement: For A perfectoid, every finite étale A°^a-algebra 𝔅 gives, after inverting ϖ, a perfectoid A-algebra B with B°^a ≅ 𝔅; conversely if B is a finite étale perfectoid A-algebra (resp. Galois with group G) then B°^a is finite étale over A°^a (resp. Galois with group G). The proof uses completeness of 𝔅 (Lemme 1.7.1), [15, th. 3.5.13 ii] to transport Frobenius, and, in the converse direction, the identification B°^a ⊗̂_{A°^a} B°^a = ∏_G B°^a from Proposition 3.3.4, then a Galois envelope with group S_r and Lemme 2.4.1(2). André notes that this Galois argument replaces the use of Robba rings in [21].

items.name: Reduction of almost purity to (∗)_A, and the sketch of its proof
items.statement: Given Proposition 3.4.2, the second equivalence of Théorème 3.4.1 amounts to (∗)_A: every finite étale A-algebra is perfectoid. In characteristic p this holds because a finite étale algebra over a perfect ring is perfect. In characteristic 0 the sketch runs: (a) (∗)_L for L/K finite; (b) the Gelfand transform Γ(A) is perfectoid, being a uniform product of the perfectoid fields ℋ(x), so B⊗_AΓ(A) is perfectoid and spectral; (c) Γ(A♭) ≅ Γ(A)♭, the ℋ(x)♭ are uniform colimits of rational localizations A♭_α of A♭ and ℋ(x) of their untilts A_α, which are rational localizations of A, giving an essentially commutative square of equivalences whose verticals are ♯ and whose horizontals are Elkik-style approximation; (d) compactness of ℳ(A) gives a finite cover by rational localizations over which B becomes perfectoid, and one descends by the sheaf properties of perfectoid algebras. Part (2) of the theorem then follows from part (1), from Théorème 3.3.2 and from Grothendieck’s remarkable equivalence.
items.note: Step (c) is printed with "les basculés A_α qui sont des localisations rationnelles de A♭"; the A_α are the untilts and are rational localizations of A (source issue E9). The sketch invokes prop. 3.7.1, rem. 3.6.4 and prop. 3.8.1, proved later; André asks the reader to check that no vicious circle arises.

items.name: Perfectoid algebras over a non-perfectoid p-adic base
items.statement: Over a p-adic field K not assumed perfectoid one may call a uniform Banach K-algebra A perfectoid when Frobenius is surjective on A°/p and there is ϖ_{1/p} with ϖ_{1/p}^p ≡ p mod p²A°; this gives elements of norm |p|^s for every s∈Z[1/p] and A°°=(A°°)², and there are analogues of the tilting equivalence, of Proposition 3.3.4 and of Théorème 3.4.1, with almost étale understood in the setting (A°,A°°). The "uniform algebras" of [21] are the paper’s spectral algebras.

items.name: Ramified complete regular local rings admit perfectoid covers
items.statement: Every ramified complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field is W(k)[[T_{≤n}]]/(p−f) with f in the square of the maximal ideal and not divisible by p, and W(k)[[T_{≤n}^{1/p^∞}]]^/(p−f) is perfectoid in the generalized sense. Extracting p-power roots of a regular sequence that does not generate the maximal ideal need not give a perfectoid algebra, as R=Z₂[[T]][√(T²+4)] with the sequence (2,T) shows.

items.name: B° is the integral closure of A° in a finite étale extension
items.statement: For B a finite étale extension of a perfectoid K-algebra A, B° is integral over A° and is in fact the (complete) integral closure of A° in B. The proof reduces to constant rank r, writes the characteristic polynomial χ_b(T)=Σ(−1)^i Tr_{∧^iB/A}(·b)T^{r−i}, and uses that B°^a is almost finite projective over A°^a so that the traces lie in A°^a_*=A°; the second assertion follows with Lemme 2.4.1(1). When A has finitely many connected components one may instead pass to a Galois closure and apply Lemme 2.4.1(2).

items.name: Descent of perfectoidness along a finite étale extension
items.statement: If a perfectoid K-algebra B is a finite étale extension of a sub-K-algebra A, then A is perfectoid: one reduces to the Galois case and applies Proposition 3.8.1 on invariants. André notes this partial converse is not used in the sequel.

items.name: Extremal quotients of perfectoid algebras are perfectoid
items.statement: The embedding K-Perf → K-uBan is faithful with a right adjoint, so it preserves and reflects epimorphisms. Since K-Perf is coreflective with monomorphic adjunction counits, it is stable under extremal quotients: for B perfectoid and φ:B→C an extremal epimorphism of uniform Banach K-algebras, C is perfectoid — though viewed as an epimorphism of perfectoid algebras φ need not be extremal.

items.name: A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid
items.statement: For A a spectral perfectoid K-algebra and g∈A°, the canonical A⊗̂_K K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is an extremal epimorphism from a spectral perfectoid algebra, so A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid; writing g♭ for the inverse system of the g^{1/p^k} modulo p one has g = #g♭.

items.name: Dense images, surjectivity and the canonical factorisation
items.statement: If φ:B→C has dense image and B is perfectoid then C is perfectoid; if moreover φ is surjective and B spectral, the spectral norm of C is the quotient norm and the induced map of unit balls is almost surjective. Hence φ is surjective iff φ♭ is, the condition being almost surjectivity of φ° mod ϖ, identified with φ♭° mod ϖ♭. Since ker φ♭ is a closed radicial ideal, B♭/ker φ♭ is perfectoid and φ factors in K-Perf as B → (B♭/ker φ♭)♯ → (B/ker φ)^u → C with the first surjective, the second simultaneously an extremal epimorphism of uniform Banach algebras and a monomorphism. André states these results are not used in the sequel.

items.name: The affinoid localization of K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩
items.statement: For char K = 0, taking ϖ of the form #(ϖ♭) and ϖ^{1/p^i} := #((ϖ♭)^{1/p^i}), the tilt of K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and one computes, level by level and in the completed colimit, K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T}° = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞},(ϖ^j/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ (3.12), the unit ball K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T}_{≤1} = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞},ϖ^j/T⟩ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⊗̂_{K°⟨T⟩}K°⟨T,ϖ^j/T⟩ (3.13), and K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T} = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⊗̂_{K⟨T⟩}K⟨T⟩{ϖ^j/T} (3.14). By (3.12) this is perfectoid, hence uniform, but by (3.13) not spectral in general. For every uniform Banach K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra A with g the image of T, A{ϖ^j/g} ≅ A⊗̂_{K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩}K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T} (3.15).

items.name: Affinoid localizations of a perfectoid algebra at ϖ^j/g
