items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra with its spectral norm and g = T·1. For every j, A{ϖ^j/g} is perfectoid and (A°⊗̂_{K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩}K°⟨T^{1/p^∞},(ϖ^j/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩)_* ≅ A{ϖ^j/g}° (3.16); in particular A⊗̂_{K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩}K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/g}^u is spectral. For char K = 0, A{ϖ^j/g}♭ is identified with A♭{(ϖ♭)^j/g♭}.
items.note: The first clause is printed A{ϖ^j/T} and the rest A{ϖ^j/g}; since g = T·1 by hypothesis the mathematics is unaffected.

items.name: Rational localizations of a perfectoid algebra are perfectoid
items.statement: The same argument gives that A{f₁,…,f_n/g} is perfectoid whenever the f_i and g admit compatible systems of p^m-th roots; it is true without that hypothesis, Scholze deducing it by an approximation of f_i, g ∈ A° by elements #f̃_i♭, #g̃♭.

items.name: Uniform products and the Gelfand transform of a perfectoid algebra
items.statement: Uniform products of perfectoid algebras are perfectoid, because (∏A^{αo})/ϖ ≅ ∏(A^{αo}/ϖ). If A is perfectoid so is its Gelfand transform Γ(A), and Γ(A♭) ≅ Γ(A)♭: Γ(A) is a uniform product of the fields ℋ(x), each a uniform colimit of rational localizations of A hence perfectoid, and the second assertion follows from the commutation of rational localizations with tilting together with ℳ(A) ≅ ℳ(A♭). For A not perfectoid, Γ(A)♭ can be much larger than Γ(A♭), as for A = K⟨T⟩.

items.name: K-Perf is complete, and what its limits are
items.statement: The category of perfectoid K-algebras is complete, because K-uBan is complete and K-Perf is coreflective in it. In characteristic p the embedding also has a left adjoint and so reflects limits: perfectoid limits are the uniform limits, and ♭ commutes with ulim. In characteristic 0 one obtains them by tilting: perfectoid limits are ulim^♮.

items.name: Perfectoid limits differ from uniform limits already for finite limits
items.statement: In characteristic 0 perfectoid and uniform limits do not coincide, already for finite limits: the intersection of two perfectoid subalgebras of a perfectoid algebra need not be perfectoid, as Â_∞[√g] = (completion of Q(A_∞))(√g) ∩ Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩ shows for p=2, n=1, g=T+4.

items.name: Invariants under an infinite group need not be perfectoid
items.statement: Proposition 3.8.1 does not extend to infinite groups: the Galois action of Z_p on T₁^{1/p^∞} extends by continuity to Â_∞, but the algebra A₀ of its invariants is not perfectoid.

items.name: The tilt of a perfectoid limit
items.statement: For char K = 0 with ϖ = #(ϖ♭), the perfectoid limit of a projective system of perfectoid K♭-algebras is their uniform limit. For a system of perfectoid K-algebras with uniform limit A, the perfectoid limit is A♮, whose tilt is determined by (A♮)^{♭o} = A^{♭o} = lim_F A° = lim_{F,α}A^{αo} = lim_α A^{α♭o} = lim_{F,α}(A^{αo}/ϖ) (3.17); A♮ → A is not an isomorphism in general.

items.name: A uniform limit of perfectoid algebras that is not perfectoid
items.statement: With p=2, n=1, g=T+4: by Théorème 4.2.2 the uniform limit of the Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩⟨ϖ^j/g⟩ is g^{−1/2^∞}Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩, the complete integral closure of Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩ in its localization at g; passing to 2Z₂-invariants, the uniform limit of the invariants is the complete integral closure of Â_∞[√g] in Â_∞[√g,1/g]. Since Â_∞ is completely integrally closed and the integral closure of a completely integrally closed ring in an algebraic extension of its fraction field is again completely integrally closed, that limit is Â_∞[√g], which is not perfectoid.
items.locator: Exemple prophylactique 3.8.5, p. 52; [8, ch. V, §1, ex. 14]

items.name: K-Perf is cocomplete
items.statement: The category of perfectoid K-algebras has filtered colimits, namely the uniform colimits, since Frobenius stays surjective on colim(B_α^{oa}/ϖ) ≅ (ucolim B_α)^{oa}/ϖ (3.18); having also amalgamated sums ⊗̂^u = ⊗̂, it is cocomplete, colimits being computed as in K-uBan and commuting with tilting.

items.name: Completed algebraic extensions and infinite coproducts
items.statement: The completion of an algebraic extension of a perfectoid field K is the uniform colimit of the finite separable subextensions, each perfectoid, hence perfectoid. The coproduct of a family of perfectoid K-algebras is the completed tensor product ⊗̂_α B_α, and for every perfectoid B the morphism ⊗̂_{α∈B^{♭o}}K⟨T_α^{1/p^∞}⟩ → B, T_α ↦ #α, has dense image.

items.name: The p-adic Riemann extension theorem
items.statement: By the Riemann extension theorem bounded analytic functions on a complex polydisc minus a hypersurface g=0 extend to the polydisc; the p-adic analogue holds: with A = K₀°[[T₁,…,T_n]] = W(k)[[T_{≤n}]] and A₀ = A[1/p], one has A = lim_j A₀{ϖ^j/g}° (4.1) for every non-zero g∈A. Perfectoid versions of this statement are the object of §4.
items.locator: §4, opening, p. 53; [4] Bartenwerfer, quoted without a statement number

items.name: A short proof of the unit-ball form of the extension theorem
items.statement: The weaker statement A = lim_j A₀{ϖ^j/g}_{≤1} (4.2) has a short proof: after a change of variables one may take g in Weierstrass form in T_n, so that A/gA ≅ ⊕_{s<r}K₀°[[T_{<n}]]T_n^s and, by Nakayama, A = ⊕_s K₀°[[T_{<n},g]]T_n^s; applying ⊗_{K⟨g⟩_{≤1}}K⟨g,p^j/g⟩_{≤1} and killing p-primary torsion gives a compatible decomposition of A₀{p^j/g}_{≤1}, which reduces the claim to g = T_n, handled by expanding in powers of T_n. Passing to the uniform colimit to reach the perfectoid algebra Â_∞ "ne va pas de soi"; that is taken up in Exemple 4.2.6, where the equality with A₀{ϖ^j/g}° is also proved.
items.locator: §4.1, formula (4.2), p. 53; [8, VII, §3, n. 7 lemme 3 and n. 8 prop. 5]

items.name: Almost perfectoid envelopes of affinoid algebras
items.statement: Let B be a reduced affinoid K-algebra of dimension n. Choose a Noether normalisation making B a finite extension of A := K⟨T_{≤n}⟩, and choose g ∈ A° such that B[1/g] is étale over A[1/g]. Let 𝒜 be the almost perfectoid algebra g^{−1/p^∞}K⟨T_{≤n}^{1/p^∞},g^{1/p^∞}⟩ and let ℬ be the integral closure of B⊗_A𝒜 in B⊗_A𝒜[1/g]. Then ℬ is almost perfectoid by Proposition 5.3.1, and ℬ^{oa} is finite étale over 𝒜^{oa} modulo every power of p, in the setting (K°[T^{1/p^∞}],(ϖT)^{1/p^∞}K°[T^{1/p^∞}]) via T^{1/p^k} ↦ g^{1/p^k}. If Question 3.5.1 has a positive answer then 𝒜 and ℬ are even perfectoid. This attaches perfectoid algebras to an arbitrary reduced affinoid algebra, where previous constructions were confined to toric situations governed by the logarithmic form of Faltings’ almost purity theorem.
items.note: The hypotheses are choices: the Noether normalisation, and an element g with B[1/g] étale over A[1/g], whose existence the paper does not argue here. The perfectoidness of 𝒜 and ℬ is conditional on Question 3.5.1 (p. 46), which the paper leaves open in characteristic 0. The tensor products are printed uncompleted.
